mechanisms.name: Continuous-batching schedule step
mechanisms.trigger: every engine step, from the busy loop
mechanisms.observable: RUNNING requests get tokens first, then WAITING ones are admitted, within the token budget, max_num_seqs and free KV blocks; a SchedulerOutput lists new and cached requests, tokens per request and finished ids
mechanisms.note: Budget is always max_num_batched_tokens: max_num_scheduled_tokens, max_num_active_seqs and the separate input_budget with draft_slots are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Step output application
mechanisms.trigger: after each executed step, once per scheduled step in FIFO order
mechanisms.observable: sampled tokens are appended, drafts rolled back, stops detected, finished requests freed, and per-client EngineCoreOutputs with stats returned
mechanisms.note: Skips invalid_block_ids and failed_recving handling, pooler outputs, num_nans, aux outputs, finished_requests sets, connector stats and KV event publication.

mechanisms.name: Preemption on KV exhaustion
mechanisms.trigger: allocate_slots returns None for a RUNNING request
mechanisms.observable: the tail request (FCFS) or worst (priority, arrival) request frees its blocks, resets num_computed_tokens to 0, returns to the waiting head and is recomputed; no waiting request is admitted that step
mechanisms.note: The early breaks are missing: a connector with pending block frees, and a victim whose blocks can only be freed later. requires_kv_delivery drop mode is also absent.

mechanisms.name: Request state machine
mechanisms.trigger: add_request, each step, stop, abort
mechanisms.observable: a request moves WAITING (or blocked) to RUNNING, PREEMPTED and back, then to a FINISHED_* status, and leaves the table once its blocks are freed
mechanisms.note: WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ is not a modeled transition, and aborting during an async KV load does not delay the block free.

mechanisms.name: Waiting-request admission chain
mechanisms.trigger: the WAITING pass of each step with budget left
mechanisms.observable: checks run in order: slot limit, blocked status, stale output, max_loras, prefix and connector hit, chunking, encoder budget, allocation; a skip defers one request, a failed allocation stops the scan
mechanisms.note: Omits the encoder-transfer pending check, DP prefill deferral, spec-decode padding, and connector hit reconciliation (partial tail, diverged hybrid hit).

mechanisms.name: Chunked prefill and long-prefill cap
mechanisms.trigger: a request needs more tokens than the budget, or more than long_prefill_token_threshold with others eligible
mechanisms.observable: the prefill is split over steps; with chunking off the scan stops instead; the adaptive cap never drops below a fair share of the budget

mechanisms.name: Prefix-cache hit lookup
mechanisms.trigger: admission of a request with no computed tokens
mechanisms.observable: the longest run of chained block hashes is adopted, capped at num_tokens - 1 so the last token is recomputed, and queries and hits are counted
mechanisms.note: No EAGLE last-block drop for full attention and no shared_prefix_boundary junction pin.

mechanisms.name: Block pool allocation and LRU eviction
mechanisms.trigger: allocation, free and prefix hits
mechanisms.observable: free blocks form a queue: uncached blocks return to the front, cached ones to the tail; popping a cached block drops its hash, and a hit removes it from the queue

mechanisms.name: KV slot allocation and watermark gate
mechanisms.trigger: each scheduling of a request that needs blocks
mechanisms.observable: a request gets blocks only if needed blocks plus the watermark (waiting requests only) fit in the free count; with scheduler_reserve_full_isl the whole sequence must fit first
mechanisms.note: No reserved_blocks, no remove_skipped_blocks before counting, no cross-attention encoder tokens, no retained_hit_group_ids.

mechanisms.name: Block hash chain
mechanisms.trigger: add_request and each newly full block
mechanisms.observable: each full block hash chains over the prefix and extra keys (multimodal, LoRA, salt) from a NONE_HASH seed, so equal prefixes hash equal, including across processes when the seed matches

mechanisms.name: Committing computed blocks to the prefix cache
mechanisms.trigger: allocate_slots, and async output in update_from_output
mechanisms.observable: full blocks up to the verified tokens gain hashes, so draft tokens are never cached and a later request can hit them

mechanisms.name: KV cache sizing and grouping
mechanisms.trigger: engine startup, after workers report available memory
mechanisms.observable: available memory over bytes per block sets num_blocks across groups; too little memory fails startup with the estimated max length

mechanisms.name: KV load failure policy
mechanisms.trigger: a connector reports failed_recving or invalid_block_ids
mechanisms.observable: with recompute, computed tokens truncate to the valid prefix and the request reschedules; with fail, it ends FINISHED_ERROR and bad blocks are evicted

mechanisms.name: Async remote KV load wait
mechanisms.trigger: a connector reports load_kv_async at admission
mechanisms.observable: the request holds blocks in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS until finished_recving, then caches them and is promoted; the last token is recomputed on a full hit
mechanisms.note: Only the success path runs: no failed-load branch, no replay marking, no kv_holding_waiting placement.

mechanisms.name: Scheduler KV connector hook chain
mechanisms.trigger: each request and step with a connector configured
mechanisms.observable: the connector sees new requests, matches tokens, learns the allocation, builds step metadata, receives worker output and decides whether a finished request keeps its blocks
mechanisms.note: No partial-tail finalization or registration, and no boundary-state offloads or KVConnectorBlockState.

mechanisms.name: Async load block reservation
mechanisms.trigger: admission of an async KV load
mechanisms.observable: the load is admitted only if it fits in free blocks minus what in-flight prefills still need plus spec-decode step blocks, which prevents deadlock

mechanisms.name: KV-holding waiting queue
mechanisms.trigger: a waiting request holds KV blocks
mechanisms.observable: such requests sit in a separate queue drained before waiting, so a block holder never sits behind a request whose failed allocation stops the scan

mechanisms.name: Deferred block free fence
mechanisms.trigger: finishing or preempting a request while overlapping batches run with a consumer connector
mechanisms.observable: blocks are parked behind the last scheduled step and return to the pool only after that step output is processed

mechanisms.name: Async scheduling output placeholders
mechanisms.trigger: AsyncScheduler, every scheduled decode
mechanisms.observable: placeholders stand in for tokens still in flight so the next step can schedule immediately; the max_tokens guard skips a request that is certainly done, and tokens are cached as they arrive

mechanisms.name: Stale output after preemption
mechanisms.trigger: output arrives for a request preempted while its step was in flight
mechanisms.observable: deliverable stale tokens are delivered but do not change reset counters; drop-mode stale output is discarded; resumption waits until stale output drains

mechanisms.name: Abort and external finish
mechanisms.trigger: client disconnect, shutdown or pause with abort
mechanisms.observable: unknown ids are ignored; known ones leave their queue, take the finished status and free their blocks; workers learn through finished_req_ids
mechanisms.note: delay_free_blocks for an in-flight WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS load and its finished/failed set cleanup are missing.

mechanisms.name: Stop and finish reason check
mechanisms.trigger: each appended sampled token
mechanisms.observable: EOS, a stop token, max_tokens or max_model_len, or a repeating tail past min_tokens ends the request with its finish reason and trims later tokens

mechanisms.name: FCFS or priority scheduling
mechanisms.trigger: scheduler_config.policy at construction, read in each pass
mechanisms.observable: FCFS uses a deque; priority uses a heap of (priority, arrival_time), and preemption chooses the worst running request and restores its budget

mechanisms.name: Skipped waiting requests
mechanisms.trigger: a waiting request is skipped by the scan
mechanisms.observable: it joins deferred_waiting, is put back ahead of older items in order, and is reported as skipped rather than waiting in stats

mechanisms.name: Scheduler pause states
mechanisms.trigger: sleep, pause or resume utility calls
mechanisms.observable: PAUSED_ALL schedules nothing; PAUSED_NEW admits only KV-holding waiting requests; has_requests respects the state
mechanisms.note: The schedule behavior admits nothing under PAUSED_NEW, so KV-holding requests stay stuck, unlike the code.

mechanisms.name: Prefix cache reset
mechanisms.trigger: weight update, sleep or the dev reset route
mechanisms.observable: without forcing it succeeds only with no blocks in use; forcing preempts all running requests first and fails loudly if blocks remain; the connector cache may reset too

mechanisms.name: Speculative token scheduling and rollback
mechanisms.trigger: speculative decoding on, each decode step
mechanisms.observable: draft tokens are scheduled with budget, rejected drafts roll back the computed count, and acceptance feeds stats
mechanisms.note: No uniform padding of new decodes, no dynamic K lookup and no grammar validation of drafts.

mechanisms.name: Encoder input scheduling
mechanisms.trigger: a multimodal request whose placeholders overlap the step token range
mechanisms.observable: items are scheduled within the encoder budget and cache; the token chunk is cut before an item that does not fit; references are freed after the step runs
mechanisms.note: A reused multimodal UUID with a different embed count is not rejected as an error.

mechanisms.name: Encoder embedding cache
mechanisms.trigger: encoder input scheduling and request free
mechanisms.observable: entries are reference counted by mm hash; unreferenced ones are evicted oldest first only under pressure, and evicted hashes reach workers through the scheduler output

mechanisms.name: Grammar compile wait
mechanisms.trigger: a structured-output request arrives
mechanisms.observable: the compile runs on a thread pool (inline under external_launcher); the request waits in WAITING_FOR_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_GRAMMAR and is promoted, or fails alone when the compile raises
mechanisms.note: The thread-pool executor and the inline external_launcher branch are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Structured output backend selection
mechanisms.trigger: the first structured request initializes the single backend
mechanisms.observable: xgrammar, guidance, outlines or lm-format-enforcer compile and enforce the grammar; an unknown backend raises
mechanisms.note: Guidance and lm-format-enforcer are assumed ready with no compile or validation.

mechanisms.name: Grammar state advance
mechanisms.trigger: each sampled token of a structured request
mechanisms.observable: the matcher advances; a rejected token ends the request FINISHED_ERROR; termination on a stop token is tracked
mechanisms.note: Only the xgrammar matcher exists: no rollback, no reasoning latch.

mechanisms.name: Grammar bitmask fill
mechanisms.trigger: each step with a structured request past prefill
mechanisms.observable: rows hold the allowed tokens per draft position and bonus token, filled in parallel for large batches without speculation, then the grammar rolls back draft advances
mechanisms.note: The scheduler returns only ids and draft counts, and no multi-row fill, rejection copy, rollback or parallel pool (threshold 128) exists.

mechanisms.name: Regex and schema pre-validation with timeout
mechanisms.trigger: request validation, and regex compile
mechanisms.observable: regexes the engine cannot build and overly nested schemas are rejected early; a compile running past VLLM_REGEX_COMPILATION_TIMEOUT_S raises a timed-out error

mechanisms.name: Reasoning-aware grammar start
mechanisms.trigger: a structured request with a reasoning parser and enable_in_reasoning off
mechanisms.observable: the grammar applies only after reasoning ends: earlier rows stay unconstrained and the end token latches reasoning_ended

mechanisms.name: Grammar validation of draft tokens
mechanisms.trigger: drafts arrive through update_draft_token_ids
mechanisms.observable: only the longest grammar-valid prefix of the drafts is kept, and the kept count sets the acceptable drafts

mechanisms.name: Grammar compile caches
mechanisms.trigger: grammar compilation
mechanisms.observable: xgrammar reuses its compiler cache up to VLLM_XGRAMMAR_CACHE_MB; outlines keeps an LRU of 128 or a version-stamped disk cache

mechanisms.name: KV cache event publication
mechanisms.trigger: block stored or removed, read at each update_from_output
mechanisms.observable: BlockStored and BlockRemoved events, annotated with group kind and connector events, are published as a batch to subscribers
mechanisms.note: Events are collected but scheduler.update-from-output never takes or publishes them, and zmq-event-publisher.publish has no caller, so they reach no subscriber.

mechanisms.name: SchedulerStats gauges
mechanisms.trigger: each update_from_output with log_stats on
mechanisms.observable: running, waiting, skipped and fetch-stage counts, KV usage and prefix stats feed Prometheus and the log
mechanisms.note: Missing num_kv_fetch_reqs_by_stage, connector prefix stats, eviction events, connector and EC stats and perf stats.

mechanisms.name: Prefix cache hit metrics
mechanisms.trigger: at admission, and taken at each stats build
mechanisms.observable: queries and hits accumulate per interval, with preempted re-admissions separate, and reset on each read

mechanisms.name: KV block residency sampling
mechanisms.trigger: kv_cache_metrics observability is on
mechanisms.observable: a sample of blocks reports lifetime, idle time and reuse gaps as eviction events in stats

mechanisms.name: KV capacity and max concurrency
mechanisms.trigger: after the KV config resolves at startup
mechanisms.observable: kv_cache_size_tokens and max concurrency are stored and logged, group and host-pool aware

mechanisms.name: max_model_len auto-fit
mechanisms.trigger: max_model_len -1 at startup
mechanisms.observable: binary search finds the longest length fitting every worker; the config is reduced or startup fails when not even one token fits
mechanisms.note: Only adoption of an already fitted value appears (gpu-worker-impl.update-max-model-len, async-mp-client.apply-ready-response); the search and failure do not.

mechanisms.name: KV coordinator and manager selection
mechanisms.trigger: KVCacheManager construction
mechanisms.observable: caching off gives the no-prefix coordinator, one group the unitary one, otherwise the hybrid one; each group gets the manager its spec maps to
mechanisms.note: The registry resolves a class, but allocation and lookup are hardwired to full attention and Mamba; no coordinator selection runs.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid fixed-point hit
mechanisms.trigger: a prefix lookup with several KV groups
mechanisms.observable: groups shrink the hit in turn until all agree on one length
mechanisms.note: Covers full attention and Mamba only; no sliding-window group, per-group hits or divergent connector hit.

mechanisms.name: Mamba state checkpoints
mechanisms.trigger: Mamba KV groups during prefill and cache commit
mechanisms.observable: a request gets a state block, optionally copied from a checkpoint; a full block commits a checkpoint and continues in a new state block
mechanisms.note: No prefill-checkpoint blocks, boundary-state offloads, partial-tail caching or EAGLE checkpoint drop.

mechanisms.name: Mamba aligned chunk split
mechanisms.trigger: mamba_cache_mode align, each prefill chunk
mechanisms.observable: chunks end where a reusable state must exist: block boundaries, last cacheable block, partial-tail boundary, shared-prefix junction
mechanisms.note: The interface computes the split, but scheduler.schedule never calls it, so no scheduled chunk changes.

mechanisms.name: Out-of-window block release
mechanisms.trigger: each allocate_slots for a sliding-window, ring or RSWA group
mechanisms.observable: blocks fully below the window return to the pool, replaced by the null block
mechanisms.note: Interfaces work alone but kv-cache-manager.allocate-slots never calls them, so no scheduled request releases a block this way.

mechanisms.name: Per-spec cache hit rules
mechanisms.trigger: lookup on sliding-window, chunked-local or ring groups
mechanisms.observable: a sliding-window hit needs contiguous window blocks scanned from the right; chunked-local nulls earlier chunks; the ring never hits
mechanisms.note: Each interface has only its own scenario; get-computed-blocks calls none of them.

mechanisms.name: Fine-grained hits with copy-on-write
mechanisms.trigger: hash_block_size below block_size with Mamba align
mechanisms.observable: a prompt tail registers inside a block; a hit copies that block privately before writing, with both copy ends held until the step runs
mechanisms.note: cache-partial-block has no caller; lookup never uses partial entries and no CoW copy reaches the SchedulerOutput.

mechanisms.name: Sparse prefix-cache retention
mechanisms.trigger: cache commit on sliding-window or Mamba groups with prefix_cache_retention_interval
mechanisms.observable: only blocks reachable at retained boundaries are hashed, so sparse groups do not fill the cache with blocks that can never hit

mechanisms.name: Sliding-window bounded prefix replay
mechanisms.trigger: a prefix hit on a model with replay groups (DSV41)
mechanisms.observable: the hit last window is recomputed without rewriting cached KV, a too-short hit is discarded, and a load carrying the window replays nothing

mechanisms.name: Streaming input sessions
mechanisms.trigger: a resumable request stops, or another chunk arrives under its id
mechanisms.observable: the session keeps computed output as prompt, resumes from the materialized frontier or waits in WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ holding its slot and blocks; a None sentinel ends it

mechanisms.name: DP prefill throttling
mechanisms.trigger: the DP coordinator sets throttle_prefills on a non-aligned step
mechanisms.observable: prefill compute defers to aligned steps unless the waiting queue is capacity bound, while decodes keep running
mechanisms.note: The request schema declares throttle_prefills and engine-core passes it, but the behavior ignores it.

mechanisms.name: Pipeline-parallel decode stagger
mechanisms.trigger: V2 runner with pipeline parallelism and async scheduling
mechanisms.observable: a request skips decode until pp_size steps after its last one, matching the sampled-token broadcast ring

mechanisms.name: Multi-module MTP prefill boundary
mechanisms.trigger: multi-module MTP with chunked prefill
mechanisms.observable: no chunk ends within num_prefill_lookahead of the prefill end, so drafters never read sampled drafts into trailing caches

mechanisms.name: New block zeroing
mechanisms.trigger: groups that need zeroed KV (needs_kv_cache_zeroing)
mechanisms.observable: newly allocated block ids drain each step and workers zero them before use, skipping blocks an async load will write
mechanisms.note: No skip_zeroing_group_ids and no record_blocks_for_zeroing after a failed load.

mechanisms.name: Encoder cache transfer gating
mechanisms.trigger: an EC connector with multimodal requests
mechanisms.observable: a request whose embeddings are still in transit is skipped; an unavailable input fails it retryably; the connector can delay frees

mechanisms.name: Auxiliary output routing
mechanisms.trigger: aux_output_config enabled
mechanisms.observable: routed experts per request join its EngineCoreOutput, and connector state clears on finish, preempt or reset

mechanisms.name: Diffusion scheduler variant
mechanisms.trigger: a diffusion model
mechanisms.observable: canvas placeholders are capped, drafts trimmed to canvas width, and a request with its full read in flight skips a step

mechanisms.name: Encoder-decoder cache manager
mechanisms.trigger: an encoder-decoder model such as Whisper
mechanisms.observable: nothing is cached: each input re-encodes, its slots return at request end, and its entries free one step after allocation

mechanisms.name: Tiered offload cascade
mechanisms.trigger: a GPU to primary store completes
mechanisms.observable: chunks become readable in the CPU primary, then cascade to each secondary tier allowed by backpressure, pinned until each job finishes; request-level tiers park in-flight keys
mechanisms.note: The logic mirrors the code but no OffloadingConnector calls it, so a request never reaches it; it runs only from scenarios, against the example tier, with no pending cascade keys.

mechanisms.name: Tiered promotion and lookup retry
mechanisms.trigger: lookup misses primary
mechanisms.observable: a secondary hit reserves a primary slot and is promoted in one batched load per tier and request at step end; RETRY means ask again; a full primary reads as a miss
mechanisms.note: Same as the cascade: no request path calls it, and only the example tier, which never answers RETRY, is wired in.

mechanisms.name: Secondary tier backpressure
mechanisms.trigger: each cascade store and store completion on a tier with a detector
mechanisms.observable: an EMA of seconds per MiB with water marks, warmup, idle decay, cooldown and a healthy fast path drops stores in proportion to overshoot, and drops are counted

mechanisms.name: CPU primary tier
mechanisms.trigger: offload stores and loads
mechanisms.observable: chunk slots are pinned by ref_cnt during reads, evicted LRU when ready and unpinned, and written chunks become readable on completion
mechanisms.note: Sound logic, but reachable only through the tiering manager, which no request path calls.

mechanisms.name: ARC and pluggable eviction policy
mechanisms.trigger: eviction_policy in connector config
mechanisms.observable: arc balances recency and frequency with T1/T2 and ghost lists, adapting its target; external policies load by module path

mechanisms.name: Offload spec and tier factories
mechanisms.trigger: connector config at startup
mechanisms.observable: a spec_name or tier type resolves to a registered or out-of-tree class; a duplicate name is refused; tier config is passed on, with backpressure parsed apart
mechanisms.note: Only the example and P2P tiers instantiate; fs, obj and kvcr resolve by name with no behavior behind them.

mechanisms.name: Filesystem secondary tier
mechanisms.trigger: a tier of type fs
mechanisms.observable: chunks store through a temp file and atomic rename on hash-named paths with O_DIRECT fallback; failed loads keep earlier blocks and mark only later keys as misses; instances share a root dir
mechanisms.note: Only the IO pool exists: no tier manager, FileMapper, atomic rename or partial-load miss marking.

mechanisms.name: Async tier existence lookup
mechanisms.trigger: FS or object tier lookups, flushed each step
mechanisms.observable: lookups return pending until a worker batch resolves them; stale generations drop, unwanted keys delete, and a failed lookup counts as a miss
mechanisms.note: The loop runs as a flow, but no tier calls it.

mechanisms.name: Object store secondary tier
mechanisms.trigger: a tier of type obj
mechanisms.observable: startup probes connectivity and fails on misconfiguration; NIXL transfers poll to completion, with a job held until its handle is released

mechanisms.name: KVCR secondary tier
mechanisms.trigger: a tier of type kvcr
mechanisms.observable: query, deliver and deposit run through the KVCR runtime, with framework pin serving for remote readers

mechanisms.name: Tiered cache reset
mechanisms.trigger: sleep, weight update or resume
mechanisms.observable: secondary tiers drain in-flight IO (a stuck tier blocks visibly), the primary resets, persistent tiers keep data, and backpressure detectors reset
mechanisms.note: Only the primary tier reset exists (cpu-offloading-manager.reset-cache); the drain and bookkeeping of TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache have no behavior.

mechanisms.name: P2P session handshake
mechanisms.trigger: the first message between two peers
mechanisms.observable: ConnectMsg carries NIXL metadata, block_len, config fingerprint and hash seed; a mismatch kills the connection; ConnectAck flushes queued messages; the handshake has a deadline

mechanisms.name: P2P block fetch and transfer
mechanisms.trigger: a consumer request loads from its producer
mechanisms.observable: FetchMsg records demand per round, stored blocks transfer by RDMA as they arrive, TransferDone completes the load, and an empty terminal fetch closes the id

mechanisms.name: P2P load timeout and abort
mechanisms.trigger: a load passes 30 s, or its abort passes 10 s
mechanisms.observable: the client sends AbortFetch, the server cancels and drains inflight transfers, and the load fails to local prefill; store jobs time out at 30 s

mechanisms.name: Symmetric P2P lookup and serve
mechanisms.trigger: a symmetric peer probes for a key
mechanisms.observable: LookupMsg batches flush per step; the server pins hits and parks pending keys for up to 5 s before forcing them to miss; an unanswered probe stays RETRY until finish

mechanisms.name: P2P reapers
mechanisms.trigger: every poll on the scheduler thread
mechanisms.observable: dead sessions fail their jobs and requests; unbound stores time out at 60 s and reject late fetches; idle sessions evict only when peer slots are scarce

mechanisms.name: P2P ZMQ control channel
mechanisms.trigger: connect, send and each poll
mechanisms.observable: DEALER sockets heartbeat; monitor events mark a connection dead on the first fatal event; a dead connection refuses sends
mechanisms.note: Monitor logic only, no caller: no session uses it, and heartbeats and poll are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: P2P peer session table
mechanisms.trigger: a consumer needs a producer, or a request finishes
mechanisms.observable: one bidirectional session per peer up to VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS, created with the local hash seed; a finished request closes on its session by id
mechanisms.note: Table bookkeeping only; no transfer, polling or teardown is behind it, and the tier is not wired into tiering-offloading-manager.

mechanisms.name: Simple CPU offload scheduler
mechanisms.trigger: SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, each step
mechanisms.observable: a CPU hit past the local hit pins and loads into new GPU blocks; computed blocks store to CPU; events finish on worker report and join the CPU prefix cache
mechanisms.note: Stores run only as a finish-time flush: the per-step eager selection of confirmed blocks is missing.

mechanisms.name: Lazy offload near-eviction walk
mechanisms.trigger: lazy_offload on, each step
mechanisms.observable: a cursor walks the GPU free queue and copies hashed blocks near eviction to CPU until a target number of free blocks is covered

mechanisms.name: Eager store selection
mechanisms.trigger: eager mode, each step
mechanisms.observable: only confirmed computed, stable, hashed blocks not yet stored or in flight are copied, up to CPU capacity, with per-group cursors and outcome counts

mechanisms.name: Offload worker copy launch
mechanisms.trigger: each step on the worker
mechanisms.observable: loads launch after forward to hide their overhead and stores wait on a compute-done event, then finished events report to the scheduler
mechanisms.note: The copy thread runs as a flow and registration exists; nothing launches copies from connector metadata, and the store fence is missing.

mechanisms.name: Disk offload pipeline
mechanisms.trigger: disk capacity configured
mechanisms.observable: separate store and load threads interleave staging DMA with pwritev or preadv, with O_DIRECT by default; a short IO raises
mechanisms.note: Threads run as flows, but no worker launches them; the page-cache option is not modeled.

mechanisms.name: GPU and CPU block transfer
mechanisms.trigger: offload store or load submitted on a worker
mechanisms.observable: direct or canonical copy plans become batched DMA on a stream (Triton for CPU to GPU batches above a minimum size) and finish in event order; canonical layout filters writer blocks
mechanisms.note: Every queued copy finishes by the next poll, with no copy plan, canonical layout or submitter.

mechanisms.name: Shared offload region
mechanisms.trigger: offload spec setup on scheduler and each worker
mechanisms.observable: one region maps the CPU tier; a non-creator waits up to 30 s for the file size and fails if the creator died; pinning falls back to pageable on failure
mechanisms.note: The creator wait with its timeout and dead-creator error is not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Offload connector metrics
mechanisms.trigger: each connector stats read
mechanisms.observable: tier usage, job counts, lookup latency, retries, transfer sizes and backpressure, labeled by tier, reach Prometheus through connector stats
mechanisms.note: Only the CPU chunk pool counts exist; no caller reads them, and TieringMetricsTracker is absent.

mechanisms.name: Simple offload metrics
mechanisms.trigger: each connector stats read
mechanisms.observable: save outcomes, load blocks, used and pending-store blocks and an info gauge are exported

mechanisms.name: HiSparse GPU page residency
mechanisms.trigger: each step on a HiSparse deployment
mechanisms.observable: clean GPU pages unpin once the host copy is durable and stay readable until reused; a requester without a host path asks for a hot region when the pool runs low

mechanisms.name: HiSparse host write-back and publication
mechanisms.trigger: pages completed by a scheduled request
mechanisms.observable: spills write pages to the host pool; on worker completion GPU pins drop and hashes publish once the prefix is durable, even for detached finished requests

mechanisms.name: HiSparse hot-cache top-k swap in
mechanisms.trigger: each sparse MLA decode layer
mechanisms.observable: top-k positions resolve to resident or host rows, group leaders compact and stage swaps once, and hot slots replace LRU rows

mechanisms.name: HiSparse layout and host pool
mechanisms.trigger: startup with hisparse_config
mechanisms.observable: sparse, hot and resident groups lay out over the GPU and a pinned host pool sized from config, checked against host memory
mechanisms.note: Config and connector checks exist; the group layout, host pool allocation and memory check are missing.
